title: Open-source black holes: how many projects ignore outside pull requests (October 2026) | Porchlamp

findings.text: In Porchlamp's {snapshot_id} snapshot, {black_holes} of {judged} active open-source projects ({share}%) left most outside pull requests with no human reply, review or merge within {deadline_days} days.
The share rises with stars: {band1_share}% of projects with {band1_label} stars, {band2_share}% at {band2_label}, and {band3_share}% at {band3_label}.
{top100_black_holes} of the 100 most-starred projects are black holes, and only {top100_overlap} of them reach Porchlamp's top 100.
Across {ranked} ranked projects, the rank correlation between stars and the Porchlamp score is {rho}.

findings.lead: Most of those pull requests waited.
findings.text: Inside the black-hole projects, {unanswered} of {counted} counted outside pull requests got no human reply within {deadline_days} days.

sentences.lede: The state of open-source black holes: how often a stranger's pull request goes unanswered, in the Porchlamp snapshot of {snapshot_date}.
sentences.intro: You send a small fix to a project you use every day. Two weeks later, nobody has replied.
sentences.stars_answer: They answer less often, on average. The black-hole share climbs at every step up in stars.
sentences.stars_not_charted: Not charted: {below_bands_judged} judged project with fewer than {lowest_band} stars.
sentences.ecosystems_answer: Python and JavaScript projects go quiet more often than Rust, Go, Java or C and C++ projects.
method: We followed {corpus_prs} pull requests from {corpus_authors} outside contributors to {corpus_projects} GitHub projects, from {window_start} to {window_end}.
A project is judged only when it is licensed, maintained software with at least {min_n} counted outside pull requests.

Another {undecided_rule_inputs} licensed, maintained projects with at least {min_n} outside pull requests on record are not judged yet: those records were fetched before drafts and closes were recorded, and the rules need both.
We could not judge {undecided_cut} busy projects yet: we hold only the newest {pr_cap} pull requests of each, and they do not reach back to {window_start}.

{sampled} projects had more than {full_max} pull requests in that time. For each, we read replies and reviews on an even random sample of {sample_size} of them; every pull request counts for decisions and merges.
It is a black hole when, with {ci_percent}% confidence, more than half of those pull requests got no substantive reply, review or merge within {deadline_days} days.

sentences.cite: Porchlamp ({year}). Stars don't review pull requests: the state of open-source black holes. Snapshot {snapshot_id}. {frozen_url}
sentences.stars_chart_summary: Black-hole share by stars: 17% of 2,034 projects with 1,000 to 10,000 stars; 24% of 1,844 projects with 10,000 to 50,000 stars; 27% of 246 projects with 50,000 or more stars.
sentences.ecosystems_chart_summary: Black-hole share by package ecosystem, highest first: Python 27.3% of 932; JavaScript 21.4% of 1,230; Go 18.1% of 580; Rust 17.0% of 565; C and C++ 16.5% of 558; Java 13.5% of 260.
